title: Blumenthal sets Jan 4 deadline for Binance, Tether and Trump crypto firms as power shifts
body: Traders have largely priced in the political shift. The bigger risk now is to timing: the market structure bill could slip down the agenda while the new majority prioritises investigations. Stablecoin liquidity is the pressure point to watch, because Tether sits at the centre of crypto trading. A memecoin issuer has no such role. The WLFI token and the USD1 stablecoin face the most direct reputational risk from the probe. Bitcoin and ether face only indirect, sentiment-driven exposure. --- Earlier: Bitcoin continues to trade heavily, under $74,600, risk mood turns wary --- Blumenthal has spent most of a year writing letters to crypto firms; from January his requests come with the power to compel answers. Summary: In letters announced on November 5, Senator Richard Blumenthal renewed his records demands to Binance, Tether, World Liberty Financial and Fight Fight Fight LLC World Liberty and Fight Fight Fight must start producing documents by November 30, and all four firms face a final deadline of January 4, 2027 January 4 is one day after the new Congress convenes, when Blumenthal is expected to chair the Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations As ranking member he can only request voluntary cooperation, and he has warned of further measures, widely read as subpoenas, if the firms don't comply The inquiries cover Iran-linked transfers at Binance, Tether's payments to a firm linked to Bo Hines, and the Trump family's crypto ventures Bitcoin briefly fell below $76,000 ...

title: Weekend: Houthis hit Riyadh's Aramco Tower and target oil storage as Saudi supply risk grows
body: This is an escalation risk for crude rather than a confirmed supply loss: Saudi Arabia reports minor damage and intercepted missiles, and no outage has been reported. What matters is the direction. Aramco storage is now being targeted, and the Houthis have a declared maritime embargo against Saudi Arabia, at a time when Hormuz flows are already disrupted and Saudi barrels routed via the Red Sea matter more for global supply. Coming on top of the suspected Iranian strike on Iraq's Khor Mor gas field and Rubio's warning that talks with Tehran are not productive, it strengthens the case for a firmer war-risk premium. Traders will be watching for any confirmed damage to Saudi output, storage or Red Sea loadings. --- A Houthi strike on Riyadh's financial district, with Aramco oil storage also in the crosshairs, shows the Iran war's reach now extends deep into the world's largest oil exporter, just as Saudi Red Sea exports matter most. Summary: Houthi forces struck the Aramco Tower in Riyadh's financial district on Saturday. The group said it also targeted Riyadh's airport and Aramco oil storage facilities. Saudi Arabia said several missiles were intercepted and destroyed. Saudi Arabia's energy ministry reported minor damage and no casualties, though verified footage suggests heavier damage to at least one floor. The strike followed Houthi claims that a Saudi-led coalition air strike killed at least 33 people in Yemen.

title: RBA's Hunter warns AI could trigger sharp asset repricing as boom adds to inflation
body: Hunter's description of AI as a near-term inflationary force supports the RBA's tightening bias rather than pointing to relief. That underpins the Australian dollar on rate differentials and keeps the focus on the risk of further hikes. Her financial stability warning adds a central bank voice to growing market unease over AI valuations and funding, at a time when tech-linked assets are already under strain. Any further move toward repricing would favour defensive positioning in AI-exposed equities. It could also limit the Australian dollar's upside if global risk sentiment sours. --- Last week: investingLive Asia-Pacific market news: RBA hikes to 18-year high --- The RBA sees AI as an inflation problem today and a potential financial stability problem tomorrow, with little sign yet of the productivity payoff that would justify the investment boom. Summary: RBA Assistant Governor Sarah Hunter said AI may be increasing risks to financial stability. Some asset prices could face sharp repricing, or disorderly adjustments, if returns on AI investment disappoint. There is limited evidence AI has materially lifted aggregate productivity or had large effects on employment in advanced economies. In the near term, AI-driven demand against constrained supply adds upward pressure on inflation. The long-run effect is likely broadly neutral. There are tentative signs of labour market adjustment in AI-exposed occupations, particularly for younger workers.

title: Rubio says Iran talks not productive as Tehran's demands are unacceptable
body: For oil, this is the more important signal of the weekend. Trump made avoiding renewed strikes conditional on progress in talks, and his Secretary of State now says there isn't any. That pushes escalation risk back toward the front of the market's mind and argues for a firmer war-risk premium in crude. Combined with the suspected Iranian strike on Iraq's Khor Mor gas field, the de-escalation story from Trump's CNN interview looks shakier. Traders are likely to be more cautious about selling crude on hopes of a deal. Any fresh threat to US forces or to Hormuz shipping would test Rubio's pledge to respond. Trump set progress in talks as the condition for holding off on new strikes, and his top diplomat is now saying that condition isn't being met, a shift that puts escalation risk firmly back in the frame. Summary: Rubio said negotiations with Iran are not productive because Tehran's demands are simply unacceptable. He said a diplomatic solution is sometimes not possible, though the US will keep exploring whether one exists. The US is taking defensive action and will respond if its forces in the region are threatened. Rubio stressed long-standing cross-party agreement that a nuclear-armed Iran would be completely unacceptable. The tone contrasts with Trump's weekend comments that renewed strikes were highly unlikely if talks progressed. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has said negotiations with Iran are not productive because Tehran's demands are simply unacceptable.

title: Bitcoin continues to trade heavily, under $74,600, risk mood turns wary
body: With no crypto-specific trigger, bitcoin is trading as a high-beta proxy for wider risk appetite, so tonight's Nvidia open is the key test. A heavy tech sell-off would likely keep pressure on the token. A calm open could see the dip bought. The 200-day moving average, a little above $73,000, is the next level traders are likely to defend. A clean break would put the longer-term uptrend in question. Persistent ETF outflows suggest institutional buyers aren't rushing to step in at current levels. --- Earlier: Three risks for Nvidia shares after Huang admits affair with suspected Chinese spy --- Bitcoin is drifting lower on a nervous Monday morning, with no crypto news of its own, which leaves Nvidia and Wall Street's tech mood as the likeliest guides for where the token heads next. Summary: Bitcoin fell below $75,000 early in the Asian session, trading around $74,500. No crypto-specific catalyst was evident. The move coincides with a more cautious tone across risk assets. title: Japan's Foreign Reserves Edge Higher in October, Reaching $1.179 Trillion
body: Japan's foreign exchange reserves inched up in October 2026, rising to USD 1,179.1 billion from USD 1,178.4 billion in September, according to the latest data updated on 8 November 2026. The marginal increase highlights a period of relative stability in the country's external buffers. The October uptick, while modest, suggests that Japan continues to maintain one of the world's largest reserve positions, providing a significant cushion against external shocks and currency volatility. The data will be closely watched by investors and policymakers for signals on Japan's capacity to respond to shifts in global financial conditions. title: NZX 50 Slips amid Uncertainty over Election Results
body: The NZX 50 slipped 25 points, or 0.2%, to 13,974 in early Monday trading, extending the previous session's losses amid uncertainty over the general election outcome. The November 7 general election raised the prospect of a hung Parliament, though National appears best positioned to form a coalition with ACT and New Zealand First, while a narrow victory by the opposition bloc remains possible. Analysts noted that investors were also closely watching the US midterm election results, the evolving conflict in the Middle East, and their implications for oil prices. Traders were awaiting the latest Chinese consumer and producer price data, due later in the day. A positive session on Wall Street on Friday, driven by a rebound in technology stocks, helped limit the NZ market's decline. On the local bourse, healthcare and consumer staples names were the main drag on the index, while gains in financial and energy stocks helped cushion the fall. Early notable decliners included South Port NZ (-2.0%), Fisher & Paykel (-1.2%), A2 Milk (-1.6%), and EBOS Group (-1.0%). The material has been provided by InstaForex Company - www.instaforex.com
